description: `DocAccess` and the boundaries above it catch `Forbidden`, `Unauthorized` and `RpcClientError`. `GetDoc` can also fail with `DocNotFound`, so `useDocAccess` returns `Doc | Unhandled<DocNotFound>`, and reading `.title` off it doesn't type-check until `Boundary.isUnhandled` rules the failure out.

errors.message:
Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound> | { readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }'.
  Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound>'.

title: Until every error is handled, the data can be an `Unhandled`

description: Read through `Session`, a doc can still fail with `Forbidden` or `DocNotFound`: both come back in the `Unhandled`. Forgetting one is a type error that names it.

errors.message:
Argument of type '{ DocNotFound: () => string; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ValueTagHandlers<DocNotFound | Forbidden> & {}'.
  Property 'Forbidden' is missing in type '{ DocNotFound: () => string; }' but required in type 'ValueTagHandlers<DocNotFound | Forbidden>'.

title: What's left must be matched exhaustively

description: Under `DocAccess`, the failure is `DocNotFound` and nothing else. An `Unauthorized` can't reach this component (`Session` caught it), so a case for it is a type error, not dead code.

errors.message: Type '() => string' is not assignable to type 'never'.

title: You can't handle an error a boundary already caught

description: `Session` already catches `Unauthorized`, so a boundary inside it that lists the tag again would never see one. The error names the tag.

errors.message:
Type '["DocNotFound", "Unauthorized"]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ["DocNotFound", "Unauthorized"] & { readonly AlreadyHandledAbove: "Unauthorized"; }'.
  Property 'AlreadyHandledAbove' is missing in type '["DocNotFound", "Unauthorized"]' but required in type '{ readonly AlreadyHandledAbove: "Unauthorized"; }'.

title: A boundary can't catch what one above it catches

description: `DocsClient.runtime` is built from the RPC client's layer. An atom on it that needs another service (`Analytics` here) doesn't type-check where it is made, before any boundary reads it. tsc reports it against the last overload, the `Stream` one: the `Analytics` in `Effect<number, never, Analytics>` is what the runtime lacks.

errors.message:
No overload matches this call.
  The last overload gave the following error.
    Type 'Effect<number, never, Analytics>' is missing the following properties from type 'Stream<unknown, unknown, AtomRegistry | DocsClient | Reactivity>': channel, [TypeId]

title: An atom can only use services its runtime provides

description: `Boundary.useSet(DocAccess, renameDocAtom)` sends `Forbidden`, `Unauthorized` and `RpcClientError` to the boundaries, and resolves to `Doc | Unhandled<DocNotFound | EmptyTitle>`: the new title is behind `Boundary.isUnhandled` too.

errors.message:
Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound | EmptyTitle> | { readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }'.
  Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound | EmptyTitle>'.

title: A write through a boundary narrows like a read

description: A boundary that catches `DocNotFound` too leaves nothing, so its hook returns the doc itself: no `Unhandled`, nothing to match. `useSession(docListAtom)` is the same: `Session` and the boundaries above it catch everything `ListDocs` can fail with. The fallback's `error` is the universe's `DocNotFound`, with its `docId`. This file compiles.
title: Once every error is caught, there is no failure to get

description: The root declares `AppError`, everything a `DocsClient` query can fail with, so a boundary's tags autocomplete from it, and a misspelt one is a type error with a suggestion instead of a boundary that never catches anything.

errors.message: Type '"Forbiden"' is not assignable to type '"DocNotFound" | "EmptyTitle" | "Forbidden" | "RpcClientError" | "Unauthorized"'. Did you mean '"Forbidden"'?

title: A tag must be one of the universe's

description: Boundaries match by `_tag`, so they can't tell two errors with the same tag apart. When the universe has two, say a second API's `Forbidden`, catching that tag is a type error. Tags only one error carries still work.

errors.message:
Type '["Forbidden"]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ["Forbidden"] & { readonly TagSharedByMoreThanOneError: "Forbidden"; }'.
  Property 'TagSharedByMoreThanOneError' is missing in type '["Forbidden"]' but required in type '{ readonly TagSharedByMoreThanOneError: "Forbidden"; }'.

title: A tag two errors share can't be caught

description: `DocAccess`'s fallback expects the universe's `Forbidden`, with a `docId`. An atom outside the universe that fails with its own `Forbidden` would hand that fallback a value its props don't describe, so reading it through `DocAccess` is a type error. Through `Network`, which doesn't catch `Forbidden`, it would come back as an `Unhandled`.

Argument of type 'Atom<AsyncResult<never, OrgForbidden>>' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Atom<AsyncResult<never, OrgForbidden>> & { readonly CaughtAsAnotherType: "Forbidden"; }'.
  Property 'CaughtAsAnotherType' is missing in type 'Atom<AsyncResult<never, OrgForbidden>>' but required in type '{ readonly CaughtAsAnotherType: "Forbidden"; }'.
